how_to_use: Each persona file holds a complete answer set and the expected outcome. A persona passes if the recommendation matches, the total and both category scores fall inside their ranges, the fired gates match exactly, the threshold rules match exactly, the exemptions match exactly, and the suggestion include/exclude assertions hold. Suggestion assertions are against the TRIGGERED set, not the 3-5 displayed. Separately, scripts/check-personas.mts applies one global invariant to every persona with no per-persona assertion needed: the DISPLAYED suggestion count must land between meta.selection.min_shown and max_shown (3-5) in config/suggestions/mid-b-to-high-b.json. Run with: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-personas.mts mid-b-to-high-b

field_notes.rules_expected: Threshold rules that actually applied and constrained the result. Named '<rule_id>:<question_id_or_category>' where a rule is driven by one answer or one category. Note the engine only reports a Ready-path threshold rule when the total itself reached the Ready threshold — a pilot held at Nearly ready by their total alone reports no rule. The not_yet category floors are a separate branch and ARE reported, which is why persona 09 carries one.
field_notes.exemptions_expected: Exemption ids that suppressed a rule which would otherwise have applied. Every persona here has an EMPTY exemptions list, and that is structural rather than accidental: config/scoring/mid-b-to-high-b.json ships an empty thresholds.ready.unevidenced_core_checks.exemptions array on purpose. See the negative check about carried-over exemptions below.
field_notes.critical_check_floor_ordering: The engine breaks on the first failing question in thresholds.ready.critical_check_floor.questions, so at most one 'critical_check_floor:*' string is ever emitted and WHICH one depends on list order. The order in this step's config is deliberate (most-to-least step-specific, with the two softest-sourced members last). Personas 03 and 08 both have more than one failing member and pin which string is reported.

persona_count_note: Nine files. The brief asks for 6-9 at this step and this rubric needs the upper end of that, because it has 11 gates, 10 Ready-blockers and three mechanisms that exist at no other step (the thermic-hours measure, the currency gate, and the demonstrated-readiness gate). Nothing here is a near-clone: unlike tests/personas/low-b-to-mid-b, there is no paired control persona, because this step has no stated-plans exemption to control for. If the count needs trimming, the honest candidate is 08 'nearly-froze-in-a-collapse', whose single-weak-check behaviour overlaps structurally with 07 — though it is the only persona sitting on the freeze-versus-lost-control boundary, which is this rubric's most important collapse distinction, so it is the last one worth losing.
expected_values_provenance: The score ranges in these files were computed by hand from config/scoring/mid-b-to-high-b.json (skills weights total 164, psychological weights total 84, category split 0.55/0.45). The 'computed' figures below are the hand-calculated values; each persona's asserted range is roughly plus or minus four points around them to tolerate arithmetic slip. The first run of a real scorer should reproduce the 'computed' figures to within rounding; if it doesn't, check the arithmetic here before changing the engine — but if a persona's RECOMMENDATION, gates, rules or exemptions differ, the disagreement is structural and worth investigating properly.
note_on_distribution: Fewer Ready results than at either step below (3 of 9 at low-B to mid-B, 4 of 10 at A to low-B), which is intended and matches the evidence: three manufacturers describe this tier as not for beginners or occasional pilots, and the published hours marker is specific and comparatively well corroborated. Note that all four Not yet personas have genuinely decent flying — three of them are capped by a gate while scoring in the sixties or seventies. That is the shape of a step where the demands are about currency and demonstrated need rather than about raw competence.

gate_coverage.thermic_hours_low_and_little_other_airti: Not exercised as a FIRING gate, deliberately. Persona 03 matches its thermic band (10_25) and must NOT be gated, because his total airtime is over 200 — that is the clause honouring Hamerton's ridge-soaring alternative far enough not to cap him while still not treating it as qualifying. The negative case is the more important one here. A synthetic unit check should confirm the gate DOES fire for the same thermic answer paired with total_airtime: 50_100.
gate_coverage.still_in_training: Not exercised. Close to inert two rungs up the ladder — a pilot on a mid-B shopping for a high-B is long past supervised flying — and flagged in config/scoring/mid-b-to-high-b.json meta.owner_decisions as removable. Worth a synthetic unit check rather than a persona.
gate_coverage.no_recent_flying: Not exercised. Persona 04 sits one band above it ('less than once a month'), which is the distinction that matters here: the no-flying-at-all case gates on its own, the less-than-monthly case needs a thin 12-month figure alongside it. Worth a synthetic unit check.
gate_coverage.unreliable_launches: Not exercised. No persona answers 'launch_reliability: often_aborted'; the weakest launch answer in the set is 'only on the sites and days I know well' (persona 06), which is scored rather than gated. Worth a synthetic unit check.
gate_coverage.collapse_control_lost: Not exercised, deliberately. Persona 08 sits exactly one band above it, which is this rubric's most important collapse distinction: freezing trips a Ready-blocker, losing control trips a gate. A synthetic unit check should confirm both 'lost_control' and 'repeated_struggle' cap at Not yet.
gate_coverage.instructor_said_wait: Not exercised. Mechanically identical to the same gate at both steps below, where it is already proven. Worth a synthetic unit check.

not_exercised: critical_check_floor on flying_frequency, wing_limiting_evidence, thermal_turn_control, reading_the_day, active_piloting, reserve_familiarity and response_when_rough. Several personas hold failing answers for these (06 fails active_piloting at 0.35, thermal_turn_control at 0.3, reserve_familiarity at 0.5 — on the line — and response_when_rough at 0.25; 05 fails wing_limiting_evidence at 0.15) but all of them are gated first, and gates short-circuit. Each is worth a synthetic unit check: take persona 01 and change one answer at a time, which is also the cheapest way to review the seven rule_messages those cases would render.

ready_category_floor:skills and ready_category_floor:psychological. Not reachable from any persona here. The closest is persona 07 (skills 74.0 against a floor of 70) and no persona has a lopsided-but-passing profile — persona 09, the lopsided one, falls through to the Not yet floor instead. A synthetic check should take persona 01 and weaken the psychological answers just enough to land between 65 and the Ready threshold.

not_yet_category_floor:skills. No persona falls below the floor of 45 — persona 06 is closest at 45.5 and is gated first anyway. Worth a synthetic check, and worth noting the floor was raised from 40 at the steps below, so a persona that sat at 42 would behave differently here than one rung down.
conservative_backstop. No persona leaves questions blank; every persona answers all 32.
rule_coverage.owner_decision: The un-exercised threshold rules all use logic shared with the two steps below and already proven there. What is NOT covered by these personas is whether each piece of this step's rule_messages copy reads correctly in a real result — and this step has more of that copy than either predecessor (ten critical_check_floor messages). Worth deciding between a few more personas and a synthetic copy-review pass.

suggestion_coverage.always_pool_sizing: config/suggestions/mid-b-to-high-b.json ships FOUR 'always': true suggestions on four distinct topics (instructor, currency, transition, step_confidence), one more than min_shown. Two of them can be topic-deduped by a triggered suggestion ('stay_current_whatever_you_decide' by improve_currency or recurrency_plan, 'compensate_after_any_upgrade' by transition_plan), but dedupe replaces rather than subtracts, so the displayed count never falls. Personas 04, 05 and 09 all exercise at least one of those displacements.
suggestion_coverage.thin_end_note: The thinnest trigger set in this set is persona 02 at nine triggered suggestions. A genuinely gap-free pilot with no stated ambitions would trigger five (four always plus test_fly_first), still at max_shown. The pool cannot drop below four for any answer set.
suggestion_coverage.step_confidence_suggestion: 'judge_the_wing_not_the_label' is priority 12, so it backfills rather than crowding out earned advice and most personas here will not see it displayed. That is intentional and not a coverage hole: the same honesty reaches every pilot unconditionally through always_output.methodology_note in config/scoring/mid-b-to-high-b.json and meta.confidence_statement_for_ui in config/questions/mid-b-to-high-b.json. Owner call if it should be promoted.
suggestion_coverage.high_priority_siv_suggestion: 'collapse_training_early' is priority 2 here against 7 at low-B to mid-B and 3 at A to low-B, because knowledge/disagreements.md points 8 and 12 land hardest at this step — a mid-B is realistically the last wing many pilots will own on which a collapse can be induced representatively. Personas 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07 and 08 all trigger it, which is deliberately broad. It remains non-scored; the only thing SIV touches numerically is the capped 2-point bonus.

negative_checks: No persona may be gated or band-dropped for not having done a manoeuvres course. Persona 08 reaches Nearly ready with 'manoeuvre_course: no'; persona 09 stays Not yet having done one; personas 01 and 02 reach Ready with scores that clear the threshold before the bonus is added. knowledge/disagreements.md point 1 and BRIEF.md both require SIV to be a small positive signal only.

No persona may be gated or Ready-blocked on ground handling. knowledge/disagreements.md point 11, and knowledge/steps/mid-b-to-high-b.md's finding that BHPA's own Pilot Rating Scheme page names ground handling nowhere, mean it is scored here but is neither a gate nor a Ready-blocker. Personas 05, 06 and 07 all have weak kiting and none is held by it — 05 and 06 are gated on other things, 07 by her collapse-practice answer.

A pilot who reports no collapse history must not be penalised into a lower band for it. Persona 02 answers 'collapse_experience: never' and reaches Ready; the answer scores 0.55, above the Ready-blocker line.

A pilot who regularly flies strong thermic and mountain days must not be scored DOWN for it at this step, unlike at the two below. Personas 01 and 09 both answer 'strong_mountain_big_air' and it takes a full 1.0. Three manufacturers position this class for exactly that air.

Ambition alone may never cost a band. Persona 01 ticks longer_xc and reaches Ready; persona 05 ticks longer_xc with skills at 70.8 and is not gated by it; persona 09 ticks longer_xc and competitions with skills at 96 and is not gated by it. Only persona 06, who pairs them with a skills score under 55, is.

Wanting more performance must never be penalised on its own, per knowledge/disagreements.md point 9. Personas 03, 04 and 07 all answer 'want_more_performance' on upgrade_motivation and none is gated for it; it is also deliberately absent from the motive list in the 'aspirational_rather_than_demonstrated' gate.

A comparison-driven motive must not cap a pilot whose readiness evidence is genuinely there. Persona 09 matches the 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' motive clause twice over and must NOT be gated. Persona 06 is where the same gate correctly fires, with the same kind of motive and genuinely thin skills.

No stated-plans exemption may fire at this step. Persona 03 matches the exact profile that config/scoring/a-to-low-b.json and config/scoring/low-b-to-mid-b.json would exempt — local_only plans plus a ridge/coastal conditions answer plus an untested thermalling answer — and must still be held at Nearly ready. A scorer that shares exemption logic across steps, or that falls back to a sibling step's config, will report Ready here and be wrong. This is the single most likely cross-step regression in this rubric.

An untested check must still be explained to the pilot it affects. Persona 03 asserts both 'thermalling_untested' and 'local_plans_and_this_wings_purpose' are present, so the absence of an exemption is never a silent block.

An injury or reserve deployment in the last 12 months must not cap a result on its own. No persona here answers 'incidents_12m: injury_or_reserve' — worth a synthetic check that such a pilot, otherwise strong, is NOT gated and does trigger 'post_collapse_support'. Carried forward from config/scoring/a-to-low-b.json's v2 removal of exactly that gate.

Freezing once in a collapse is not the same as falling apart under load. Persona 08 froze in a collapse and still answers 'heart rate goes up, but I carry on flying the wing' about rough air generally; 'nerves_are_not_the_problem' must not fire for her. Conflating the two would misdiagnose her and would read as a judgement on her nerve, which docs/design-context.md's tone rule forbids.

No rule or gate message may claim three independent sources agree on the ~50-hour figure. knowledge/disagreements.md point 6 reduces it to roughly two independent voices. A reviewer should read every fired message in personas 03, 06 and 07 against that specifically — the thermic-hours messages and the 'build_thermic_hours' suggestion are the three places most likely to drift.
Every pilot must reach at least three displayed suggestions. Enforced for all nine personas by the displayed-count invariant in scripts/check-personas.mts; all nine reach five.

Nothing in a Ready or Nearly ready output may read as talking a hesitant pilot into the upgrade. Persona 02 is the one to read for this — she is capable, careful and correct to be, and docs/design-context.md's safety guard forbids reassurance as a design goal. Persona 03 is the second: his result is the tool telling a strong pilot 'not for this wing, not yet', and it has to land as information rather than as a reprimand.

chain_notes.merge_behaviour: In a low-B to high-B chain (config/questions/low-b-to-mid-b.json then config/questions/mid-b-to-high-b.json), 23 of this step's 32 questions are byte-identical to their counterparts at the step below and merge into a single screen each, so the chain asks 30 + 32 - 23 = 39 questions rather than 62. The nine that deliberately do NOT merge are total_airtime, total_flights, airtime_last_12m (hours bands scale up), thermic_airtime and wing_limiting_evidence (new questions), ground_handling_kiting, speed_bar and collapse_practice (option scales extended with this step's own sourced material), and wing_expectation (names the target class in its text).
chain_notes.what_a_chain_persona_would_need_to_check: No chain persona exists for this pair yet. The two things worth asserting if one is added: (a) that a merged answer is scored against EACH step's own bands — most visibly 'active_piloting: work_brakes_actively', which scores 0.9 at low-B to mid-B and 0.7 here, and 'collapse_practice', whose absence blocks nothing one rung down and blocks Ready here; and (b) that scripts/check-merge-rule.mts is extended with this pair, including a MUST_NOT_MERGE_IDS list containing the nine ids above. The existing script covers only the a-to-low-b to low-b-to-mid-b chain.
chain_notes.source: BRIEF.md 'Multi-step jumps' and its recorded implementation trap: question ids are not safe to treat as globally shared, and the merge must compare actual option sets rather than ids.
